title: Physics-Informed Teleconnection-Aware Transformer for Global Subseasonal-to-Seasonal Forecasting

problem.claim: Global subseasonal-to-seasonal forecasting predicts climate conditions several weeks to months ahead and remains highly challenging because of chaotic atmospheric dynamics and cross-scale interactions.

gap.claim: Existing approaches often do not explicitly model the physical processes and teleconnections important at subseasonal-to-seasonal timescales.

contributions.claim: TelePiT is a deep learning architecture integrating multi-scale physics and teleconnection awareness for global subseasonal-to-seasonal forecasting.
The architecture combines spherical harmonic embedding, a multi-scale physics-informed neural ODE, and a teleconnection-aware transformer.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe TelePiT as a novel architecture that integrates multi-scale physics and teleconnection awareness.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show TelePiT significantly outperforms state-of-the-art data-driven baselines and operational numerical weather prediction systems across all forecast horizons.

narrative_sequence.summary: Subseasonal-to-seasonal forecasting supports agricultural planning, energy management, and disaster preparedness.
The task is difficult because atmospheric systems are chaotic and interact across multiple scales.
Current approaches often fail to explicitly represent relevant physical processes and teleconnections.
TelePiT addresses the gap with integrated multi-scale physics and teleconnection-aware modeling through three architectural components.
The authors report superior performance against data-driven and operational numerical forecasting baselines across forecast horizons.

source_observation.claim: The proposed architecture explicitly combines multi-scale physical-process modeling with teleconnection-aware attention.

interpretation.claim: Forecasting systems may benefit when domain structure and long-range interactions are represented as explicit model components.

application.claim: For other global spatiotemporal forecasting tasks, consider combining geometry-aware representations, multi-scale dynamics, and long-range interaction modeling.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether these components are necessary individually or jointly.

unknowns: Datasets, evaluation metrics, and numerical forecast horizons are not specified.
Ablation results and implementation details are not provided.
The reported performance is not independently verified.
